items.stem: What does the with statement provide when opening a file in Python?

options.text: It guarantees the file is closed when the block exits, even on an error
options.rationale: Correct: with uses the context-manager protocol to release the resource reliably.

options.text: It makes file reads run concurrently
options.rationale: with does not add concurrency; it manages resource cleanup.

options.text: It converts the file contents to JSON automatically
options.rationale: Parsing JSON is a separate step with the json module.

options.text: It prevents any exception from being raised inside the block
options.rationale: with still lets exceptions propagate; it only ensures cleanup happens.

items.explanation: Correct: with uses the context-manager protocol to release the resource reliably.

items.stem: Which statements about Python dictionaries are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Keys must be hashable, such as strings or numbers
options.rationale: Correct: dictionary keys must be hashable so they can be located quickly.

options.text: Looking up a value by key is on average fast regardless of size
options.rationale: Correct: dict lookups are average constant-time thanks to hashing.

options.text: Dictionaries keep values sorted by key automatically
options.rationale: Dictionaries preserve insertion order, not sorted order.

options.text: A list can be used directly as a dictionary key
options.rationale: Lists are unhashable and cannot be dictionary keys.

items.explanation: Correct: dictionary keys must be hashable so they can be located quickly.; Correct: dict lookups are average constant-time thanks to hashing.

items.stem: Why is using a mutable default argument such as def f(items=[]) a common bug?

options.text: The same list is shared across all calls that rely on the default, so state leaks between calls
options.rationale: Correct: the default is evaluated once at definition, so every call reuses and mutates the same list.
Default arguments are allowed; mutable ones are just risky.

options.text: The list is recreated on every call, wasting memory
options.rationale: The opposite is true: it is created once and reused.

options.text: It makes the function run in a separate thread
options.rationale: Default arguments have nothing to do with threading.

items.explanation: Correct: the default is evaluated once at definition, so every call reuses and mutates the same list.
